evidence.claim: The Security Council said Egypt played a crucial role in brokering the Gaza ceasefire and that the effort helped prevent a full-scale war.
evidence.title: Ceasefire Between Israel, Palestinian Militants 'Fragile', Middle East Coordinator Tells Security Council, Urging All Parties to Uphold Truce, Safeguard Past Gains
evidence.excerpt: The Security Council said Egypt played a crucial role in brokering the Gaza ceasefire and that the effort helped prevent a full-scale war.
evidence.source_locator: Special Coordinator remarks on Egypt's role
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN confirmation of Egypt's mediation role.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong corroboration of Egypt's mediation policy under Sisi.
contrary_evidence: The same passage notes the ceasefire was fragile and casualties were substantial.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the truce was mediated by Cairo after an Egyptian security source said Israel had agreed to the proposal.
evidence.title: Israel, Palestinians agree truce from Sunday evening - sources
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the truce was mediated by Cairo after an Egyptian security source said Israel had agreed to the proposal.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting on a negotiated ceasefire and Egyptian mediation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports Egyptian state mediation under Sisi; not direct presidential speech.
contrary_evidence: The report is source-based and does not independently verify the entire ceasefire architecture.

evidence.claim: Sisi stressed the importance of dialogue and diplomatic solutions to the Russia-Ukraine crisis in a call with Zelenskyy.
evidence.title: Egypt's President Sisi receives phone call from Ukrainian counterpart - presidency
evidence.excerpt: Sisi stressed the importance of dialogue and diplomatic solutions to the Russia-Ukraine crisis in a call with Zelenskyy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a dated presidential call, carried by Euronews.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributes the call to Sisi.
contrary_evidence: A phone call is rhetorical and does not by itself show follow-through.

evidence.claim: Sisi reiterated prioritising dialogue and diplomatic solutions and said Egypt was ready to support that path through bilateral and multilateral contacts.
evidence.title: Egypt calls for prioritising dialogue, diplomatic solutions to solve Ukrainian crisis: Sisi
evidence.excerpt: Sisi reiterated prioritising dialogue and diplomatic solutions and said Egypt was ready to support that path through bilateral and multilateral contacts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a presidential meeting with Lavrov.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi in a bilateral meeting with Lavrov.
contrary_evidence: State-aligned framing may understate Egypt's balancing act with Russia.

evidence.claim: Egypt voted for the resolution and said it wanted hostilities to stop and that dialogue and understanding were preferable to double standards.
evidence.title: With 143 Votes in Favour, 5 Against, General Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Russian Federation's Annexation of Four Eastern Ukraine Regions
evidence.excerpt: Egypt voted for the resolution and said it wanted hostilities to stop and that dialogue and understanding were preferable to double standards.
evidence.source_locator: Egypt statement in explanation of vote
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN record of Egypt's explanation of vote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State delegation position under Sisi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The UN text is a statement of position, not proof of operational peace policy.

evidence.claim: UN officials said Libya's constitutional-track talks were held in Cairo, that the delegations agreed on 137 of 197 articles, and that Egypt hosted the next round under UN auspices.
evidence.title: Statement by USG Rosemary DiCarlo - Security Council meeting on the situation in Libya
evidence.publisher: UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs
evidence.excerpt: UN officials said Libya's constitutional-track talks were held in Cairo, that the delegations agreed on 137 of 197 articles, and that Egypt hosted the next round under UN auspices.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN account of the Cairo-hosted negotiation track.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Egyptian hosting and facilitation are attributable to the Sisi administration, not to unilateral Libyan decisions.
contrary_evidence: The talks did not resolve all issues and Libya remained unstable.

evidence.claim: After the Cairo talks ended without agreement, the UN special adviser thanked Egypt for its hospitality during the three rounds of talks.
evidence.title: HoR-HSC Joint Committee Cairo talks end with no agreement on transition or elections
evidence.excerpt: After the Cairo talks ended without agreement, the UN special adviser thanked Egypt for its hospitality during the three rounds of talks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent local-regional reporting on the talks and the UN's remarks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports Egypt's role as host/facilitator, but not as decisive broker.
contrary_evidence: The talks ended without agreement on transition or elections.

evidence.claim: Sisi said Egypt was keen to provide all means of support to achieve political, security and economic stability in Sudan and to continue consultation on the GERD issue.
evidence.title: Sisi affirms Egypt's keenness to provide all means of support to Sudan
evidence.excerpt: Sisi said Egypt was keen to provide all means of support to achieve political, security and economic stability in Sudan and to continue consultation on the GERD issue.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement on Sudan and regional stability.
contrary_evidence: Support for a neighboring transitional authority is not the same as success in ending the crisis.

evidence.claim: Egypt and Sudan called on Ethiopia to resume serious talks under AU auspices for a legally binding GERD deal, and Egypt treated unilateral operation as a breach of international law.
evidence.title: Egypt, Sudan call on Ethiopia to actively engage in serious GERD talks to reach legally binding deal
evidence.excerpt: Egypt and Sudan called on Ethiopia to resume serious talks under AU auspices for a legally binding GERD deal, and Egypt treated unilateral operation as a breach of international law.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of an official joint statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Joint statement under Sisi's government; reflects coercive-water-security diplomacy rather than armed force.
contrary_evidence: The wording also shows hard-edged security claims that Ethiopia and others could view as pressure.

unresolved_gaps: There is no direct 2022 ruler-attributed nuclear command, safety, or crisis decision in the file.
El Dabaa evidence is mostly permits, construction milestones, and project self-reporting, not independent safety enforcement.
The package shows mediation and diplomatic statements, but not the internal decision chain or independent proof that Egypt's mediation changed outcomes.
There is little direct evidence on any offensive military option or coercive-force decision in 2022.
The chain from abuse to personal or cabinet-level accountability is thin, especially for prisons, police, and protest repression.
The limited remedial evidence is not outcome-verified; pardons and release gestures need follow-through data.
There was no live national election in 2022, so contestability and succession are inferred largely from retrospective rights reporting.
The internal effect of dialogue initiatives and jail releases on pluralism is not independently shown.
Hard verification of State Ownership Policy implementation and actual divestments by year-end is thin.
Household-level welfare effects of inflation, transfers, and bread security are incompletely tied to ruler action.
The package lacks direct ruler-level attribution for social-welfare decisions beyond ministerial and partner-mediated actions.
There is little completed-outcome evidence for 2022 on poverty, learning loss, malnutrition, and sanitation after the interventions.
Direct evidence of personal assets, beneficial ownership, procurement gains, or family enrichment is still missing.
The file has one clear public denial and several propaganda or censorship claims, but fewer independently verified false statements with explicit contradiction.
The core 2022 economic program is reconstructed from speeches, policy papers, and partial implementation steps rather than a single explicit governing program document.
Independent verification of divestment, budget execution, and durable follow-through is still thin.
